public_rationale: Growing paid enterprise adoption challenges the ordinary claim that OpenAI had failed to turn its models into products customers would buy. But the context also concerns differentiation, unbundled sales, and sustainable economics. The evidence does not settle those stronger propositions or establish the asserted causes. Calling the whole claim false solely because subscriptions existed would disregard that context.
limitations: Paid-adoption figures come from reporting of company statements, not independent customer records.
No objective killer-app threshold is supplied.
The cost accounting basis is unspecified.

our_interpretation: Assess commercialization achieved by the publication date, including the preceding product-development history described in the context.
The ordinary commercial reading of meaningful productization is a model-based product that customers repeatedly pay to use for a practical purpose.
The surrounding discussion also makes sustainable economics relevant. A product's existence or subscription sales alone cannot settle that stronger reading.
Sold separately may mean standalone paid products or individual capabilities sold outside an all-inclusive bundle. Both readings must be acknowledged.
Training costs and absent use cases are asserted causes, not conditions that must occur before a forecast can be scored.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes a broad failure to turn models into sustained commercial products and identifies high training or operating costs and insufficient useful applications as material causes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes sustained, economically viable standalone model-based products with practical customer uses, or directly refutes the proposed causes of the asserted commercialization failure.

evidence.excerpt: the number of paying enterprise users has doubled since September.
evidence.locator: Section ChatGPT sees increased enterprise and developer adoption
evidence.explanation: The report describes two million paying enterprise users and growth since September. This challenges a reading of productization as absent paid adoption, but does not establish retention, unbundled sales, or profitable economics.
OpenAI acknowledges the compute demands of advanced capabilities while announcing a paid product. It does not quantify costs or establish that they prevent meaningful commercialization.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Contemporaneous product-level economics, retention and customer-use evidence, together with records showing whether costs or insufficient useful applications prevented commercialization.
